Location:  Redwood City, CA — hybrid, at least three days per week in the office
Employment:Full-time
The role
Quilt's mission is to move homes away from fossil fuel heating. We build heat pumps and software that make efficient electric heating and cooling a better experience for homeowners.
We're looking for a software engineer who can build dependable test infrastructure and contribute to the device software it validates. Your work will help us ship reliable software for products people depend on in their homes.
Your initial focus will be making device-software testing repeatable and useful: building automation in Python, connecting tests to real hardware, and giving engineers clear feedback on their changes. You'll own the testing workflow and work with firmware, systems, cloud, and mobile engineers to choose meaningful coverage, investigate failures, and improve testability. As AI accelerates development, these systems will help the team validate changes quickly and confidently.
You'll bring practical C++ skills to this work, making changes to device software that improve its reliability and make it easier to test. As automation reduces manual effort, there will be room to take on broader device-software contributions. This is a hands-on role combining software development, infrastructure, and work with physical devices.
What you'll do
Build and maintain automated tests, reusable tools, and infrastructure for connected devices.
Make hardware testing repeatable and integrate it into development and CI workflows.
Design coverage for important customer experiences and failure scenarios, using simulation, integration tests, and real devices where each is most useful.
Investigate failures across software, hardware, and connectivity, working with other engineers to implement fixes and regression tests.
Improve test reliability, reduce manual effort, and turn results into a clear picture of release readiness.
Develop and test C++ changes that improve device-software reliability and testability, with room for broader product contributions as automation matures.
What you bring
Strong software engineering skills and experience building maintainable automation or comparable systems.
Experience writing and debugging Python and C++, with the ability to apply those skills in unfamiliar codebases.
Experience making automated tests and CI workflows reliable and useful to other engineers.
Sound judgment about system-level testing: what to test, how to test it, and how to interpret the results and their limits.
Strong debugging skills in Linux environments, including processes, networking, and logs.
Comfort working with physical devices and investigating problems across hardware and software.
The ability to drive work independently, coordinate with others, and communicate findings clearly.
Relevant experience can come from software engineering, infrastructure, robotics, embedded systems, or test engineering. We don't require a particular degree or a fixed number of years of experience.
Experience that would help
Building hardware-in-the-loop systems, automated device labs, or device simulators.
Embedded software development or testing connected-device provisioning, updates, and recovery.
Familiarity with test frameworks and build tools such as pytest, gtest, or Bazel.
Working at Quilt
This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Redwood City, with at least three days per week in the office. Relocation assistance is not available.  The expected base annual salary range for this role is $150,000–$200,000, depending on experience. In addition to base salary, Quilt also offers meaningful equity and top-tier health benefits.

**Description**
 Amazon Devices (Lab126\) builds products and services that delight millions of customers globally. The Edge AI ML Platform and Infrastructure team is building the platform that enables Amazon teams to train, optimize, evaluate, and deploy generative AI models on devices and in the cloud.
   

  

 Today, optimizing a large model for a new hardware target requires experts to connect model onboarding, distributed training, compression, evaluation, compilation, and deployment systems by hand. We are turning that work into a repeatable, self\-service workflow. Our platform supports large language, vision, audio, multimodal, and mixture\-of\-experts models, and gives scientists and engineers the tools to move new optimization techniques from research code into reliable production workflows.
   

  

 We are looking for a Software Development Manager to build and lead the ML infrastructure team behind this platform. You will own distributed training on multi\-node GPU clusters, compute capacity and utilization, CI/CD, observability, and operational reliability for GPU\-intensive workloads. You will hire and develop a team of software and ML infrastructure engineers, set its technical direction and roadmap, and deliver platform capabilities that scientists and product teams depend on to ship models with hundreds of billions of parameters.
   

  

 This role combines people leadership with deep technical judgment. You will grow engineers and managers\-in\-the\-making, drive architecture decisions with your senior engineers, turn ambiguous science and product needs into a prioritized plan, and hold a high bar for delivery and operational excellence.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Build, lead, and grow a team of software and ML infrastructure engineers: recruit and hire, set clear goals, coach for growth, and manage performance across the team.
   

  

 Own the roadmap for ML infrastructure—distributed training, GPU capacity, workflow orchestration, CI/CD, and observability—balancing near\-term deliveries with long\-term platform health.
   

  

 Drive the architecture of distributed training capabilities (data, tensor, pipeline, and model parallelism) for large language and multimodal models, partnering with senior engineers and applied scientists.
   

  

 Establish operational excellence for production platform services, including metrics, alarms, runbooks, on\-call processes, and root\-cause correction of recurring issues, while owning GPU fleet efficiency, capacity planning, and cost optimization.
   

  

 Partner with applied science, compiler, runtime, hardware, security, and product teams to align requirements, manage dependencies, and deliver cross\-team programs.
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 You will move between people, planning, and technology. A typical day might include a 1:1 with an engineer on a growth plan, a design review for a new training\-orchestration capability, triage of a failed multi\-node training run, a capacity review against upcoming model deliveries, and a planning session with science leads on next quarter's priorities.
   

  

 You will use performance, reliability, cost, and developer\-productivity data to decide where the team invests. You will deliver incrementally while protecting long\-term architecture, and make sure the team fixes recurring problems at their root.

 The Edge AI ML Platform and Infrastructure team brings together software engineers, ML infrastructure engineers, and GPU performance specialists.  The team owns the platform foundations that connect model development to deployment. Because our scope runs end to end, we can improve training, compression, evaluation, and deployment as one system. We value clear interfaces, measurable performance, automated quality gates, and direct collaboration between science and engineering.

**Description**
 AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3\) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2\), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS, including support for customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.
   

  

 Do you want to work on a product that can do the following?:
   

  

 Access petabytes of data in single\-digit milliseconds
   

  

 Replicate tables across continents
   

  

 Stream terabytes of data updates per hour continuously
   

  

 Back up hundreds of terabytes of data in seconds
   

  

 Encrypt petabytes of data with no performance degradation
   

  

 Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service that does all this and more. DynamoDB is a key\-value and document database that delivers single\-digit\-millisecond performance at any scale. DynamoDB can store petabytes of customer data and handle peaks of more than 20 million requests per second.
   

  

 As a fast growing service at the core of the AWS Cloud, our business and engineering decisions have widespread impact across AWS, Amazon, and beyond. Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission\-critical workloads.
   

  

 DynamoDB is one of the largest distributed database systems in the world, and we continue to believe it is Day 1 for the DynamoDB business. We are constantly improving and adding new capabilities to DynamoDB, and we are looking for a deeply technical, team\-first software development engineer to push DynamoDB even further.
   

  

 DynamoDB engineers are constantly challenged to think of unique and innovative solutions. The quality bar is high. As an engineer here, you will work on the hardest engineering problems in distributed systems at a massive scale and on multiple dimensions. You will exercise your intellectual curiosity, work with motivated teams of sharp individuals, and get insightful guidance from senior and principal engineers.
   

  

 This is a hands\-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Design, build, and operate distributed infrastructure systems that provision, bootstrap, and manage the DynamoDB test cluster fleet. Specifically:
   

  

 Own systems end\-to\-end. Take a problem from design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing operation. No handoffs — you build it, you run it, you improve it based on production data.
   

  

 Deliver independently with minimal guidance. Break down ambiguous problems into executable plans. Your manager sets direction; you figure out the how and drive to completion.
   

  

 Debug complex distributed systems issues. Trace failures across multiple services, accounts, and regions. Identify root causes — not just symptoms — and fix them structurally.
   

  

 Write production\-quality code in Python and Java. Ship weekly. Maintain high standards for testing, monitoring, and operational readiness.
   

  

 Operate the fleet on\-call. Triage tickets, respond to alarms, and use what you learn operationally to drive reliability improvements back into the systems.
   

  

 Collaborate across teams. Engage partner teams to unblock dependencies, review designs, and align on technical approaches. Communicate clearly in writing and in person.
   

  

 Influence technical direction. Propose improvements, write design docs, and participate in architecture decisions. You're expected to have opinions backed by data and advocate for them.
   

  

 Mentor junior engineers and interns. Review code, give constructive feedback, and help others grow.
   

  

 In short: You will be a self\-sufficient engineer who can independently own a major workstream, operate what they build, and make the engineers around them more effective.
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 Your morning starts with a message: "My test environment won't come up." By 10am you've traced a deployment failure to a race condition between two services, shipped a fix, and unblocked a team of engineers whose pipeline is green again.
   

  

 By noon, you're designing automation that lets any engineer spin up a fully functional multi\-region DynamoDB test environment with a single command — replacing what used to take a week of manual configuration. You're thinking about cross\-region networking, security boundaries, and making complex infrastructure invisible to its users.
   

  

 After lunch, you're debugging a circular dependency that's been silently generating tickets for months. You find it, fix it, and close an entire class of failures.
   

  

 What makes this role different: You're building the infrastructure that lets every DynamoDB team validate their features before they ship to customers. When you make test environments faster and more reliable, you multiply the velocity of hundreds of engineers.
   

  

 The problems are deeply technical — distributed systems orchestration, fleet management, cross\-account security, credential rotation at scale — but you'll ship code every week and see immediate impact.
   

  

 The team is small (6 engineers), the scope is large, and the ownership is real. You'll design, build, and operate entire systems end\-to\-end. You'll work with Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, CloudFormation, EC2 fleet management, IAM, Python, and Java. You'll use AI coding tools daily.
   

  

 Every major DynamoDB launch validates on infrastructure your team builds. You make that possible.

**About Nametag**
 Nametag helps companies verify the real person behind high\-risk workforce actions, from account recovery to identity checks, before attackers can exploit the gap.
   

  

 Deepfakes, social engineering, and stolen credentials have made "who is actually on the other side of this request?" a critical infrastructure problem. We are building the identity verification and account protection layer companies use to answer that question quickly, securely, and with less friction for real users.
   

  

 The Role
   

  

 We are looking for a Full Stack Engineer to build the integrations that put Nametag inside the systems our customers already use.
   

  

 Nametag is rarely the application someone opens. It's the identity check that happens inside a helpdesk ticket, an HR onboarding flow, or a Slack message from someone claiming to be the CFO. Our reach is determined by how well we embed into Workday, ServiceNow, Slack, Okta, ICIMS, UKG, and the long tail behind them — and that embedding is engineering work.
   

  

 This is a full stack role with an unusual center of gravity. You'll write backend services and APIs on our side, configuration and setup experiences in our console, and the connector code that talks to a dozen platforms that each made different decisions about authentication, extensibility, and what a webhook means. You'll join a dedicated team whose purpose is expanding Nametag into new systems and new use cases.
   

  

 What makes this work interesting is that you're building into environments you don't control and can't change. Every target platform has its own auth model, its own rate limits, its own review process, and its own idea of how much UI you're allowed. Workday's extensibility surface is narrow and governed. Slack gives you modals and Block Kit, which were not designed for identity verification. ServiceNow gives you enough rope to break a customer's upgrade path. Designing something that is secure, usable, and actually buildable inside those limits — and that keeps working when the vendor ships a change you didn't ask for — is the core of the job.
   

  

 The breadth is real. You'll be reading someone else's API documentation most weeks, and debugging behavior that documentation doesn't describe. Engineers who like going deep on one system for a year will be unhappy here. Engineers who like landing in an unfamiliar platform and having it figured out by Thursday will do well.
   

  

 You'll work closely with the product manager for integrations, who owns how each integration should work, and you'll have real influence over that design because you're the one who knows what the platform will actually permit.
   

  

 What You'll Do
   

  

**Build integrations end to end**
 Design and build connectors into third\-party enterprise platforms: authentication, data flow, event handling, and the verification experience inside the host application.
   

  

 Build the Nametag\-side APIs, services, and webhooks each integration depends on.
   

  

 Build the console configuration and setup experience customers use to install and operate the integration.
   

  

 Take integrations through marketplace and app review processes, including the requirements that gate a listing.
   

  

**Work across unfamiliar platforms**
 Get productive fast in APIs and extensibility models you haven't seen before, and develop real expertise in the ones that matter most.
   

  

 Implement against OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, and whatever a given platform does instead of those.
   

  

 Handle the operational reality of depending on other people's systems: rate limits, partial outages, breaking changes, and undocumented behavior.
   

  

**Own reliability across the fleet**
 Operate what you build. Integrations fail in production in ways that are specific to one customer's configuration, and you'll be the one who figures out why.
   

  

 Build the observability that makes a broken integration visible to us before it's visible to the customer.
   

  

 Design for versioning and backwards compatibility. Customers do not upgrade on your schedule.
   

  

**Make each one faster than the last**
 Factor shared infrastructure out of individual connectors so common patterns stop being rebuilt.
   

  

 Contribute to the tooling, scaffolding, and templates that shorten time to first working integration.
   

  

 Document how each integration works well enough that support and solutions engineers can operate without you.
   

  

 What We're Looking For
   

  

 Work authorization required: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future need for visa sponsorship.
   

  

 You do not need to match every bullet. We care most about breadth, pragmatism, and comfort working against systems you don't control.
   

  

* 4\+ years building and operating production software, including backend services and APIs.
* Demonstrated experience integrating with third\-party APIs in production — not a one\-off script, but something you owned and kept running.
* Strong backend skills in Go, Node.js, Python, Java, or similar, plus enough frontend ability to build configuration and setup UI in React or a comparable framework.
* Working knowledge of OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, webhooks, and the failure modes each brings.
* Relational database experience, PostgreSQL preferred.
* Cloud experience, AWS preferred.
* The temperament for integration work: patience with other people's documentation, and the instinct to verify rather than trust it.
* Clear communication and good judgment in a remote, cross\-functional team.


 Bonus Points
   

  

* Hands\-on experience with Workday, ServiceNow, Slack, Okta, Entra, ICIMS, or UKG extensibility specifically.
* Experience shipping an app through a marketplace or app review process.
* Experience with identity, authentication, account recovery, fraud prevention, or compliance\-heavy products.
* Experience building an integration platform or connector framework rather than individual integrations.
* Experience in a solutions engineering, professional services, or customer\-facing engineering role.


 What We Value
   

  

* **High ownership.**

**About Nametag**
 Nametag helps companies verify the real person behind high\-risk workforce actions, from account recovery to identity checks, before attackers can exploit the gap.
   

  

 Deepfakes, social engineering, and stolen credentials have made "who is actually on the other side of this request?" a critical infrastructure problem. We are building the identity verification and account protection layer companies use to answer that question quickly, securely, and with less friction for real users.
   

  

 The Role
   

  

 We are looking for a Full Stack Engineer to build the integrations that put Nametag inside the systems our customers already use.
   

  

 Nametag is rarely the application someone opens. It's the identity check that happens inside a helpdesk ticket, an HR onboarding flow, or a Slack message from someone claiming to be the CFO. Our reach is determined by how well we embed into Workday, ServiceNow, Slack, Okta, ICIMS, UKG, and the long tail behind them — and that embedding is engineering work.
   

  

 This is a full stack role with an unusual center of gravity. You'll write backend services and APIs on our side, configuration and setup experiences in our console, and the connector code that talks to a dozen platforms that each made different decisions about authentication, extensibility, and what a webhook means. You'll join a dedicated team whose purpose is expanding Nametag into new systems and new use cases.
   

  

 What makes this work interesting is that you're building into environments you don't control and can't change. Every target platform has its own auth model, its own rate limits, its own review process, and its own idea of how much UI you're allowed. Workday's extensibility surface is narrow and governed. Slack gives you modals and Block Kit, which were not designed for identity verification. ServiceNow gives you enough rope to break a customer's upgrade path. Designing something that is secure, usable, and actually buildable inside those limits — and that keeps working when the vendor ships a change you didn't ask for — is the core of the job.
   

  

 The breadth is real. You'll be reading someone else's API documentation most weeks, and debugging behavior that documentation doesn't describe. Engineers who like going deep on one system for a year will be unhappy here. Engineers who like landing in an unfamiliar platform and having it figured out by Thursday will do well.
   

  

 You'll work closely with the product manager for integrations, who owns how each integration should work, and you'll have real influence over that design because you're the one who knows what the platform will actually permit.
   

  

 What You'll Do
   

  

**Build integrations end to end**
 Design and build connectors into third\-party enterprise platforms: authentication, data flow, event handling, and the verification experience inside the host application.
   

  

 Build the Nametag\-side APIs, services, and webhooks each integration depends on.
   

  

 Build the console configuration and setup experience customers use to install and operate the integration.
   

  

 Take integrations through marketplace and app review processes, including the requirements that gate a listing.
   

  

**Work across unfamiliar platforms**
 Get productive fast in APIs and extensibility models you haven't seen before, and develop real expertise in the ones that matter most.
   

  

 Implement against OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, and whatever a given platform does instead of those.
   

  

 Handle the operational reality of depending on other people's systems: rate limits, partial outages, breaking changes, and undocumented behavior.
   

  

**Own reliability across the fleet**
 Operate what you build. Integrations fail in production in ways that are specific to one customer's configuration, and you'll be the one who figures out why.
   

  

 Build the observability that makes a broken integration visible to us before it's visible to the customer.
   

  

 Design for versioning and backwards compatibility. Customers do not upgrade on your schedule.
   

  

**Make each one faster than the last**
 Factor shared infrastructure out of individual connectors so common patterns stop being rebuilt.
   

  

 Contribute to the tooling, scaffolding, and templates that shorten time to first working integration.
   

  

 Document how each integration works well enough that support and solutions engineers can operate without you.
   

  

 What We're Looking For
   

  

 Work authorization required: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future need for visa sponsorship.
   

  

 You do not need to match every bullet. We care most about breadth, pragmatism, and comfort working against systems you don't control.
   

  

* 4\+ years building and operating production software, including backend services and APIs.

We partner with builder teams to minimize security risks across their applications while being a business enabler. Our team develops security tooling and automation to provide high quality security findings earlier in development lifecycle. We are responsible for defining and executing on the security and privacy requirements across the entire organization.
   

  

 We are looking for a Security SDE to join Amazon's Corporate Services Security team. As a security technical subject matter expert, you will engage with business, product, and technology leaders to drive security solutions at scale by partnering with senior engineers on the team. You will partner closely with our development and security teams to produce innovative and secure solutions.
   

  

 Our customers demand high standards, so a passion and discipline around security and delivery is critical. A high level of ownership and accountability is essential.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Build AI\-powered security tools and automation end to end: Contribute to technical vision, design, and delivery at large\-scale, protecting Amazon Corporate Customers. Contribute to architectural direction and high judgment decisions that shape the roadmap. Leverage Agentic AI development best practices to accelerate every phase.
   

  

 Cross\-team technical leadership: Drive execution across multiple teams and stakeholders. Decompose complex, ambiguous problems into actionable plans, unblock dependencies, and deliver cross\-team initiatives on time and at quality.
   

  

 Champion AI\-assisted secure SDLC practices: Contribute to the team's AI first development workflows including agentic coding and experimental techniques. Under the guidance of senior engineers, drive adoption, measure impact on security, velocity and quality, and set the standard for the whole team.
   

  

 Security and technical direction: Partner with senior security engineers, researchers, principal engineers, and senior leadership to translate customer security needs into technical requirements. Influence roadmap priorities with data and technical insight.
   

  

 Contributing to building the foundation for the team: Under the guidance of the senior engineers, establish development best practices, and technical review processes that set the bar for all future work.
   

  

 Mentor and grow engineers: Develop junior engineers through pairing, design reviews, and hands on coaching. Foster a culture of ownership and continuous learning.
   

  

 Contribute to operational excellence: Own security of your services. Lead on call rotations, drive root cause analysis, and implement systemic improvements.
   

  

 Innovate with urgency: Prototype security solutions rapidly, validate with customers, and iterate. Bring a builder's mindset to an environment where the best idea wins.
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 As a Software Security Engineer, you will collaborate with application development teams to ensure we keep our customers safe while developing novel services using GenAI. In a given day, you might be inspecting an application’s code, building a new framework to help our software developers build faster and more securely, or fine\-tuning the software design for a new service. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with an ability to lead by influence and communicate clearly. Technically, this person will be a software specialist with deep expertise within software development combined with security know. They will clearly articulate risks to technical and non\-technical audiences alike. Successful candidates will effectively harmonize disparate opinions while effectively prioritizing risks to guide their partners towards secure solutions.
   

  

 The Corporate Services Security (CPSS) Product Security Team is responsible for securing the applications, infrastructure and data developed across People eXperience and Technology (PXT), Finance \& Global Business Services (FGBS), Legal and Communications and Corporate Responsibility (CCR).  Do you want to help millions of customers protect their cloud workloads? The AWS security services team is building the next generation of security monitoring products that give customers a unified view of threats, risks, and compliance across multiple cloud environments. **About Parasail**
 Parasail is building the AI Supercloud, helping AI teams deploy and scale inference across a distributed network of GPUs. We make it easier for developers to bring AI applications into production with the performance, reliability, and flexibility they need.
   

  

 We’re looking for 2027 graduates who love building software, are curious about AI, and want to work directly with the people using what they build. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll help customers turn ideas into working applications—and use what you learn to make Parasail better.
   

  

**The Impact You’ll Have**
 You’ll work at the intersection of software engineering, AI infrastructure, and customer problem\-solving. Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll help customers understand their requirements, build and test solutions, and bring real workloads into production.
   

  

 You’ll write code, investigate technical problems, and see firsthand how your work affects a customer’s product. You’ll receive guidance and mentorship while taking on increasing ownership of projects from initial discovery through deployment.
   

  

 Example projects may include:
   

  

* Customer integrations: Build integrations and example applications that connect customers’ products to Parasail’s inference platform.
* Prototypes and evaluations: Turn a customer’s use case into a working prototype, then evaluate model quality, latency, throughput, and cost against their needs.
* Production deployments: Help customers move from a successful experiment to a reliable deployment, working through issues such as concurrency, retries, streaming, and error handling.
* Performance investigations: Reproduce and diagnose issues across application code, API integrations, and inference workloads, partnering with engineering to resolve them.
* Reusable developer tools: Turn lessons from customer projects into examples, documentation, and tooling that help the next developer get started faster.


 You’ll also bring customer feedback into product and engineering discussions, helping the team identify improvements that benefit many users.
   

  

**What You’ll Bring**
* Completing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field in 2027, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience building software through coursework, internships, research, open\-source contributions, or personal projects.
* Proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Python, TypeScript, or Go.
* A foundation in software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, APIs, testing, and debugging.
* Clear written and verbal communication, with an interest in explaining technical ideas and understanding other people’s goals.
* Resourcefulness when facing an unfamiliar problem: you ask thoughtful questions, test assumptions, and follow through.
* Curiosity about AI models, inference, and what it takes to run AI applications in production.
* Enthusiasm for working directly with customers and collaborating in a fast\-moving startup.


 We don’t expect you to arrive as an expert in AI infrastructure. We’re looking for strong fundamentals, evidence that you enjoy building, and a willingness to learn.
   

  

**Helpful, But Not Required**
* Projects using LLMs, open\-source models, or inference APIs.
* Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, Linux, containers, or distributed systems.
* Experience measuring application performance or evaluating model outputs.
* Experience helping others solve technical problems through teaching, tutoring, technical communities, or customer\-facing work.


**Why Join Parasail?**
* Build for real users. Work directly with developers and see your contributions become part of their applications.
* Learn across the stack. Develop practical experience in AI applications, inference infrastructure, and production engineering.
* Grow through ownership. Take on meaningful projects with support from experienced teammates.
* Help shape the product. Turn what you learn from customer deployments into improvements to Parasail’s platform and developer experience.


 If you’re excited to build, learn quickly, and help developers bring AI into production, we’d love to hear from you.

**About Nametag**
 Nametag helps companies verify the real person behind high\-risk workforce actions, from account recovery to identity checks, before attackers can exploit the gap.
   

  

 Deepfakes, social engineering, and stolen credentials have made "who is actually on the other side of this request?" a critical infrastructure problem. We are building the identity verification and account protection layer companies use to answer that question quickly, securely, and with less friction for real users.
   

  

 The Role
   

  

 We are looking for a Full Stack Engineer to build the integrations that put Nametag inside the systems our customers already use.
   

  

 Nametag is rarely the application someone opens. It's the identity check that happens inside a helpdesk ticket, an HR onboarding flow, or a Slack message from someone claiming to be the CFO. Our reach is determined by how well we embed into Workday, ServiceNow, Slack, Okta, ICIMS, UKG, and the long tail behind them — and that embedding is engineering work.
   

  

 This is a full stack role with an unusual center of gravity. You'll write backend services and APIs on our side, configuration and setup experiences in our console, and the connector code that talks to a dozen platforms that each made different decisions about authentication, extensibility, and what a webhook means. You'll join a dedicated team whose purpose is expanding Nametag into new systems and new use cases.
   

  

 What makes this work interesting is that you're building into environments you don't control and can't change. Every target platform has its own auth model, its own rate limits, its own review process, and its own idea of how much UI you're allowed. Workday's extensibility surface is narrow and governed. Slack gives you modals and Block Kit, which were not designed for identity verification. ServiceNow gives you enough rope to break a customer's upgrade path. Designing something that is secure, usable, and actually buildable inside those limits — and that keeps working when the vendor ships a change you didn't ask for — is the core of the job.
   

  

 The breadth is real. You'll be reading someone else's API documentation most weeks, and debugging behavior that documentation doesn't describe. Engineers who like going deep on one system for a year will be unhappy here. Engineers who like landing in an unfamiliar platform and having it figured out by Thursday will do well.
   

  

 You'll work closely with the product manager for integrations, who owns how each integration should work, and you'll have real influence over that design because you're the one who knows what the platform will actually permit.
   

  

 What You'll Do
   

  

**Build integrations end to end**
 Design and build connectors into third\-party enterprise platforms: authentication, data flow, event handling, and the verification experience inside the host application.
   

  

 Build the Nametag\-side APIs, services, and webhooks each integration depends on.
   

  

 Build the console configuration and setup experience customers use to install and operate the integration.
   

  

 Take integrations through marketplace and app review processes, including the requirements that gate a listing.
   

  

**Work across unfamiliar platforms**
 Get productive fast in APIs and extensibility models you haven't seen before, and develop real expertise in the ones that matter most.
   

  

 Implement against OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, and whatever a given platform does instead of those.
   

  

 Handle the operational reality of depending on other people's systems: rate limits, partial outages, breaking changes, and undocumented behavior.
   

  

**Own reliability across the fleet**
 Operate what you build. Integrations fail in production in ways that are specific to one customer's configuration, and you'll be the one who figures out why.
   

  

 Build the observability that makes a broken integration visible to us before it's visible to the customer.
   

  

 Design for versioning and backwards compatibility. Customers do not upgrade on your schedule.
   

  

**Make each one faster than the last**
 Factor shared infrastructure out of individual connectors so common patterns stop being rebuilt.
   

  

 Contribute to the tooling, scaffolding, and templates that shorten time to first working integration.
   

  

 Document how each integration works well enough that support and solutions engineers can operate without you.
   

  

 What We're Looking For
   

  

 Work authorization required: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future need for visa sponsorship.
   

  

 You do not need to match every bullet. We care most about breadth, pragmatism, and comfort working against systems you don't control.

* Working knowledge of OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, webhooks, and the failure modes each brings.

* Cloud experience, AWS preferred.
* The temperament for integration work: patience with other people's documentation, and the instinct to verify rather than trust it.

**Job Description**
* Responsible for the iteration of the underlying architecture of the large model inference engine and end\-to\-end GPU performance optimization, through means such as operator fusion and compilation optimization, deeply optimizing GPU memory access, computing pipeline, and Stream asynchronous scheduling, eliminating inference computing bottlenecks, improving single\-card inference throughput, and reducing inference latency.

* Follow up on cutting\-edge technologies such as global large model inference, GPU high\-performance computing, distributed parallelism, and cache optimization, benchmark against mainstream inference frameworks such as vLLM and TensorRT\-LLM, complete the implementation of solutions and technological innovation, continuously iterate and optimize the performance and cost advantages of the inference system, and build the core technological barriers of the team.

**About Salesforce**
 Salesforce is the \#1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
   

  

 Ready to level\-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
   

  

**About The Team**
 Accessibility is one of the hardest problems in software: it touches every component, every developer, and every user, and it's historically been slow, manual, and reactive. The Component Accessibility Team (CAT) is changing that.
 **We improve accessibility by focusing on the developer experience: we build AI tools that shift accessibility as far left as possible, so developers don't have to be accessibility experts to write perfectly accessible code.**
 We build the accessibility agent as a
 *product* 
 : the knowledge, the fix tools, and the evaluation systems that let any Salesforce engineer request and receive accessible code suggestions in the flow of their work. Our tools ship into the surfaces developers already use: AI Expert Suite, DX MCP, Cursor, Claude Code, and Vibes. When a developer writes a component, we make it WCAG\-compliant before the code makes it to production.
   

  

 This is a business problem, not only an ethical one. By improving accessibility at Salesforce we help win deals. It unlocks the features sales needs to close public\-sector and enterprise contracts, and it protects Salesforce from a fast\-growing wave of legal and regulatory risk. Accessibility serves the 1\.3 billion people worldwide who live with disabilities, and it's increasingly a condition of doing business: ADA digital\-accessibility lawsuits have increased every year since 2018, and VPAT conformance is now a standard requirement in enterprise and public\-sector procurement. The US federal government can't buy software that fails Section 508, and the EU's European Accessibility Act extended the same bar to Europe in June 2025\. Accessible\-by\-default code is how Salesforce keeps winning deals in the public sector, including with agencies that serve millions of veterans who have disabilities.
   

  

 The CAT accessibility product is already running at scale. Our Prizm PR\-review presubmit is live on core and offcore and has reviewed 42,845 pull requests since late May. Engineers acted on 21% of its findings, and only 1% were ever reported incorrect. When this team gives an accessibility recommendation, it's almost always right, and it's landing in engineers' pull requests thousands of times a week.
   

  

 What the Team Is Responsible For
   

  

* Creating products that increase developer productivity — turning accessibility from a manual, after\-the\-fact audit into an automated, in\-loop part of writing code.
* Guiding the company's web development efforts as the WCAG lead — ensuring compliance with accessibility guidelines and best practices across Salesforce's UI.
* Owning the full detect → diagnose → fix → verify loop: we don't stop at finding violations. We generate the fix, prove it holds on the rendered page, and drive it to a merged pull request.
* Ensuring AI solutions for accessibility are grounded in WCAG and internal standards — and heavily evaluated so that every suggestion the agent makes is trustworthy and high\-performing.


 What You'll Build
   

  

* Well\-evaluated AI fix tools — the Jest remediation tool, the functional\-test (ftest) remediation tool, and the accessibility\-guide tool that let developers request and receive accessible code suggestions based on the work in front of them.
* The agent's knowledge base — accessibility (a11y) best practices, remediation patterns, and Salesforce engineering standards that ground every suggestion in real WCAG success criteria.
* The evaluation system — the eval dataset and reviewer set (Aura \+ LWC) that prove, per WCAG criterion, that our AI performs before we ship it. If it isn't measured, it doesn't go out.
* The shared platform capabilities: component identification (mapping a rendered finding back to the exact component and source file it came from) and verification (confirming a semantic fix actually holds on the rendered accessibility tree).
* Detection for the dark corners of WCAG: first\-ever automated coverage for categories like reflow (1\.4\.10\) and focus management (2\.4\.3, 2\.4\.7\) that no static check can reach.
* Packaging and adoption — getting the agent into the surfaces developers live in (AI Suite, DX MCP, Cursor, Claude Code, Vibes) and driving real usage, backed by the Iron metrics dashboard.


 What You'll Do
   

  

**Build and evaluate AI\-powered accessibility tools**
* Develop fix tools and agent skills that generate, validate, and repair accessible code across Aura and LWC.
* Design and expand the eval dataset and reviewer set so we can prove correctness per WCAG criterion — not just anecdotally, but with hard numbers.
* Treat evaluation as a first\-class deliverable: no AI capability ships without a measured, defensible quality bar.


**Ground the work in real accessibility standards**
* Encode WCAG success criteria and Salesforce internal standards into the agent's knowledge so suggestions are correct by construction.
* Expand per\-criterion coverage and grow the reviewer set to close the gap between what tools can detect and what they can fix.


**Ship into developer workflows and drive adoption**
* Package tools into the Claude surfaces developers already use, and remove friction so accessibility happens automatically, not as a chore.
* Remediate real Sa11y test failures (e.g., in Matrix) and feed what you learn back into the tools.


 What We're Looking For
   

  

* Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of shipping (years of experience scale by level — AMTS early\-career through SMTS senior).
* Proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript and modern web development; familiarity with at least one component framework (LWC, Aura, React, Vue, etc.).
* A quality mindset: you reach for tests, metrics, and evaluation to prove something works — you don't ship on assumptions alone.
* Clear written and verbal communication; you can explain a technical tradeoff to engineers and to non\-experts.


**Preferred Qualifications**
* Hands\-on experience with AI/LLM\-assisted development — building agents, tools, MCP integrations, prompts, or evals (LangSmith or similar eval tooling a plus).
* Working knowledge of web accessibility — WCAG 2\.2, ARIA, screen readers, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast.
* Familiarity with the Salesforce UI ecosystem (LWC, Aura, Base Components) and testing frameworks (Jest, Selenium/functional tests).
* Experience with developer\-tooling adoption, telemetry, or metrics\-driven product work.


 Why This Role Is Unique
   

  

* Purpose you can feel. Your code makes Salesforce's products usable by people with disabilities — millions of them. This is accessibility at platform scale.
* You're defining a new discipline. We're inventing how AI does accessibility. There's no playbook — you help write it, grounded in real standards and real evaluation.
* Massive leverage. Ship a tool once; every UI engineer at Salesforce gets more accessible code by default.
* AI at the center, not bolted on. You'll work with agents, evals, and Claude\-based surfaces as your primary toolkit — and rigorously prove they perform.
* Company\-wide voice. As the WCAG lead, this team's standards shape web development across Salesforce.

 JavaScript, TypeScript, LWC \& Aura, Jest, Selenium/functional tests, WCAG 2\.2 / ARIA, AI agent \& eval tooling (Claude, MCP, Cursor, LangSmith), AI Suite, DX MCP.

**About The Video Agent Team**
 Video Agent turns a prompt, a document, or a handful of assets into a finished video. Behind a simple chat box sits a multi\-step AI agent. It plans a storyboard, writes the script, chooses avatars, voices, and visuals, calls many tools along the way, and hands the result to our rendering pipeline. Customers use it every day to make training videos, product explainers, marketing content, and more.
   

  

 We are a small team that owns the agent end to end. That covers the prompts and tools the agent uses, the backend services that run it, and the product screens where people chat with it and edit what it makes.
   

  

 This is not a role where you only call someone else's model through an API. HeyGen trains its own models in house, and the agent is built on top of them. You will work directly with those models and with the researchers who build them, which is an experience few applied AI roles offer.
   

  

**About The Role**
 You will make Video Agent better at doing what the user actually asked for, and you will prove it with data. Some weeks that means redesigning a tool the agent calls. Other weeks it means building an eval, running an A/B test, or shipping a new editing experience in React. You will own features from the first idea through launch and follow\-up, and you will decide which problems belong to the model and which belong to plain, deterministic code.
   

  

 What you'll do
   

  

* Build the agent. Design the tools, prompts, and context the agent works with. Improve how it plans, how it recovers from mistakes, and how it handles long, multi\-turn conversations.
* Measure quality. Build evals and offline replays of real sessions. Run experiments behind feature flags and read the results honestly. Watch real user sessions and agent traces to find where things go wrong.
* Ship across the stack. Build user\-facing features in TypeScript and React. Build backend services and long\-running workflows in Python and Go.
* Work closely with others. Partner with product managers, designers, and the research and rendering teams that the agent depends on.


 What we're looking for
   

  

* You have built and shipped an AI agent that real people use. We mean a system where a model calls tools, plans across several steps, and acts on the results. A chat wrapper or a prompt demo is not enough on its own. We want to hear what broke in production and how you fixed it.
* You know how to tell whether an AI system got better. You have built evals or test sets for model behavior. You can tell a real improvement from noise, and you are skeptical of results that look too good.
* You are a strong full\-stack engineer. You have 2 or more years of professional experience. You are fluent in TypeScript and React on the frontend and Python on the backend.
* You have strong product sense. You use what you build, you care how it feels, and you look at how customers actually use it.
* You take ownership. You do not wait for a spec. You find the most important problem, fix it, and tell people what changed.


 A degree in computer science or a related field is welcome but not required. Equivalent experience counts.
   

  

 Nice to have
   

  

* You have fine\-tuned models before.
* You have worked on code\-to\-video models, which generate video by writing code such as HTML or animation scripts.
* You have worked on video agent models in general.


 Show us an agent you've built
   

  

 With your application, please include a short note (a few sentences is fine) about an agent you have built. Tell us what it does, how you measured whether it worked, and one failure you found and fixed. A link to code, a demo, or a write\-up is a bonus.

**Description**
 Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. AWS Database Services provides a broad range of purpose\-built database services for any scale. Whether you need relational, key\-value, document, in\-memory, graph, time series, wide column, or ledger databases, AWS has the right database for your needs. As a member of the AWS Database organization, you'll support the development and management of database services that power millions of active customers and handle trillions of transactions.
   

  

 Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service that does all this and more. DynamoDB is a key\-value and document database that delivers single\-digit\-millisecond performance at any scale. DynamoDB can store petabytes of customer data and handle peaks of more than 20 million requests per second.
   

  

 As a fast growing service at the core of the AWS Cloud, our business and engineering decisions have widespread impact across AWS, Amazon, and beyond. Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission\-critical workloads.
   

  

 DynamoDB is one of the largest distributed database systems in the world, and we continue to believe it is Day 1 for the DynamoDB business. We are constantly improving and adding new capabilities to DynamoDB, and we are looking for a deeply technical, team\-first software development engineer to push DynamoDB even further.
   

  

 DynamoDB engineers are constantly challenged to think of unique and innovative solutions. The quality bar is high. As an engineer here, you will work on the hardest engineering problems in distributed systems at a massive scale and on multiple dimensions. You will exercise your intellectual curiosity, work with motivated teams of sharp individuals, and get insightful guidance from senior and principal engineers.
   

  

 This is a hands\-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Design, build, and operate distributed infrastructure systems that provision, bootstrap, and manage the DynamoDB test cluster fleet. Specifically:
   

  

 Own systems end\-to\-end. Take a problem from design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing operation. No handoffs — you build it, you run it, you improve it based on production data.
   

  

 Deliver independently with minimal guidance. Break down ambiguous problems into executable plans. Your manager sets direction; you figure out the how and drive to completion.
   

  

 Debug complex distributed systems issues. Trace failures across multiple services, accounts, and regions. Identify root causes — not just symptoms — and fix them structurally.
   

  

 Write production\-quality code in Python and Java. Ship weekly. Maintain high standards for testing, monitoring, and operational readiness.
   

  

 Operate the fleet on\-call. Triage tickets, respond to alarms, and use what you learn operationally to drive reliability improvements back into the systems.
   

  

 Collaborate across teams. Engage partner teams to unblock dependencies, review designs, and align on technical approaches. Communicate clearly in writing and in person.
   

  

 Influence technical direction. Propose improvements, write design docs, and participate in architecture decisions. You're expected to have opinions backed by data and advocate for them.
   

  

 Mentor junior engineers and interns. Review code, give constructive feedback, and help others grow.
   

  

 In short: You will be a self\-sufficient engineer who can independently own a major workstream, operate what they build, and make the engineers around them more effective.
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 Your morning starts with a message: "My test environment won't come up." By 10am you've traced a deployment failure to a race condition between two services, shipped a fix, and unblocked a team of engineers whose pipeline is green again.
   

  

 By noon, you're designing automation that lets any engineer spin up a fully functional multi\-region DynamoDB test environment with a single command — replacing what used to take a week of manual configuration. You're thinking about cross\-region networking, security boundaries, and making complex infrastructure invisible to its users.
   

  

 After lunch, you're debugging a circular dependency that's been silently generating tickets for months. You find it, fix it, and close an entire class of failures.
   

  

 What makes this role different: You're building the infrastructure that lets every DynamoDB team validate their features before they ship to customers. When you make test environments faster and more reliable, you multiply the velocity of hundreds of engineers.
   

  

 The problems are deeply technical — distributed systems orchestration, fleet management, cross\-account security, credential rotation at scale — but you'll ship code every week and see immediate impact.
   

  

 The team is small (6 engineers), the scope is large, and the ownership is real. You'll design, build, and operate entire systems end\-to\-end. You'll work with Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, CloudFormation, EC2 fleet management, IAM, Python, and Java. You'll use AI coding tools daily.
   

  

 Every major DynamoDB launch validates on infrastructure your team builds. You make that possible.

**Description**
 Amazon Security Lake is a fully managed security data lake service that automatically centralizes security data from AWS environments, SaaS providers, on\-premises sources, and third\-party products into a purpose\-built data lake, normalizing it to the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) so customers get a single, analytics\-ready view of their security posture across their entire organization. Security Lake operates across AWS commercial and GovCloud Regions and is trusted by many of the world's largest enterprises with their most sensitive data.
   

  

 We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to serve as a technical leader for Security Lake and across the broader AWS Security Services organization. This role is unusual in its breadth: beyond owning the architecture and operational excellence of a security\-critical, customer\-facing data service, you will lead critical\-path initiatives across our portfolio — including Amazon Security Hub and Amazon Inspector services. You will regularly be the senior engineer who lands in an unfamiliar codebase, earns the trust of another team's engineers, and converts an ambiguous business problem into a shipped, production system. If you want the reach of a platform role combined with the hands\-on depth of a service team, this is that job.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Lead the design of major deliverables end\-to\-end — from working backwards on ambiguous requirements, through design documents and security reviews (threat models, AppSec, operational readiness), to implementation, launch, and production operation
* Serve as a technical leader across AWS Security Services: embed with partner teams (Amazon Inspector, AWS Security Hub, AWS Config), deliver on their critical path to their standards and release calendars, and hand over cleanly with documentation, tests, canaries, and runbooks
* Own and raise the operational bar for Security Lake: root\-cause high\-severity issues to resolution, harden APIs and canaries, drive down recurring alarms, and keep a security\-critical service healthy and efficient
* Set technical direction and simplify: promote re\-use and extension over new components, pay down architectural debt, and turn one\-off solutions into durable practices the whole team adopts
* Drive decisions across team boundaries — when a dependency has no fix, propose the options, build consensus among stakeholders, and unblock the launch
* Mentor and grow engineers through thorough (but kind) code and design reviews, onboarding of new team members, and raising the performance bar with every review


 A day in the life
   

  

 Most of your time is spent doing hands\-on engineering: designing, writing, and reviewing code for distributed data\-processing and control\-plane systems (primarily Java and Python services with TypeScript/CDK infrastructure). In a typical week you might author a design for a new cross\-service security capability and drive it through review with senior engineers from two other teams, ship code into a partner team's codebase, dig into a production alarm and turn the root cause into a fix plus a runbook, and give design feedback that changes the direction of a teammate's approach. You will share the team's on\-call rotation and own customer issues to resolution — customers trust this service with their security data, and operational excellence is everyone's job, with senior engineers setting the example. The team is compact, senior\-leaning, and geographically distributed, which means high autonomy, direct access to Principal Engineers and leadership across AWS Security Services, and visible ownership of everything you ship.
